mainEntity.name: Can I sleep with my acrylic dentures in?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most dental professionals advise removing acrylic dentures overnight. This allows the gum tissues underneath to rest and recover, as they are under pressure during the day when the denture is in use. Wearing dentures continuously — without breaks — has been associated with a higher risk of denture stomatitis, a fungal condition affecting the gum tissue. Soaking the denture overnight also helps with hygiene and maintenance. However, individual circumstances vary, and your dentist can advise you on what is appropriate based on your specific situation.

mainEntity.name: How often should I replace my acrylic denture?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no single answer, as this depends on individual factors including how well the denture has been maintained, how much the underlying bone and gum tissue have changed over time, and the original quality of the appliance. Many dentures are reviewed every five years or so, with relining or rebasing possible as an intermediate step before full replacement. If your denture no longer fits comfortably, feels loose, or is visibly worn or damaged, it is worth having a professional assessment to determine the most appropriate course of action.

mainEntity.name: What soaking solution should I use for acrylic dentures?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cold water alone is acceptable for short-term soaking and overnight storage. Effervescent denture-soaking tablets dissolved in cool water offer the added benefit of helping to remove plaque, staining, and odour-causing bacteria. Various brands are available at pharmacies. It is important to always follow the product instructions and rinse the denture thoroughly under running water before reinserting it, as residual soaking solution may irritate the gum tissue. Your dental team can recommend a product suitable for your specific denture material.

mainEntity.name: Why does my denture smell even after cleaning?

acceptedAnswer.text: Persistent odour from a denture is usually caused by microbial colonisation — bacteria and fungi can become embedded within the porous acrylic material over time, particularly if cleaning has not been thorough. Switching to a dedicated denture soaking solution, increasing the frequency of brushing, and ensuring all surfaces including the fitting surface are cleaned properly may help. If odour persists despite improving your routine, it is worth mentioning to your dentist, as a professional clean and assessment of the denture's condition may identify the underlying cause.

mainEntity.name: Can I repair a cracked acrylic denture at home?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is strongly advisable not to attempt home repairs using household glues, superglue, or adhesives. These products are not designed for use in the mouth, may be harmful if ingested, and can make professional repair significantly more difficult or impossible. A cracked or broken denture should be assessed by a dental professional or clinical dental technician as soon as possible. Many denture repairs can be completed relatively quickly by a professional, and the result is far more likely to be safe, comfortable, and durable than any home-based attempt.

mainEntity.name: How does wearing dentures affect the remaining gum and bone?

acceptedAnswer.text: After tooth loss, the underlying jawbone naturally begins to resorb gradually over time. This process continues whether or not a denture is worn, although the rate and pattern can vary between individuals. As the bone changes shape, the fit of the denture may be affected, which is why regular professional reviews are important for denture wearers. Good denture hygiene and giving the gum tissues rest periods — particularly overnight — helps maintain the health of the tissue that supports the denture.
